newsitem.title: USA: CME hogs and pork bellies mostly up before report.
newsitem.headline: CME hogs and pork bellies mostly up before report.

text.p: CME hog and pork belly futures generally posted gains ahead of the monthly USDA Cold Storage report with weather concerns reinforcing gains in hogs, traders said.
Lean hogs closed 0.100 cent per lb lower to 0.475 higher with July up 0.025 at 81.950 cents. Pork bellies ended 0.075 to 0.175 higher with July up the least at 81.500 cents.

Expectations of continued light packer demand for hogs next week were generally offset by concern hot and humid weather would cut hog runs. Positions squaring ahead of the report also kept prices in a narrow range, traders said.

Indications for cash hogs on Monday were steady, a departure from earlier projections that cash hogs would be pressured by ample supplies. Hot weather can be stressful to hogs if they are transported, and such concerns could curb hog movement. If it lasts for several days, such weather could cut hog weights, sources noted.

The upcoming USDA Hogs and Pigs report also limited interest in trading, they said. Early analyst estimates on next Friday's quarterly data put all hogs on farms on June 1 at 102 to 104 percent of last year. Kept for breeding numbers ranged from 103 to 106 and kept for market 101 to 105 percent.

Persistant buying by Rand Financials and Rosenthal Collins offset local selling pressure. Rand also bought July and Saul Stone bought October lates. In hog options, volatility was down in July as commission houses sold 82 to 84 calls, pit sources said.

Pork belly futures ranged on both sides of previous levels after the early wide price swings as the market awaited the cold storage report. Futures traded in a 3.600 cent range, basis July, in the first few mintues as stop orders were touched off in both directions and futures had to go to resting orders before turning around, traders said.

Analyst estimates on the Cold Storage report for frozen pork bellies in U.S. warehouses as of May 31 ranged from 53.7 to 57.7 million lbs. This compares with 63.5 million lbs on hand last year and the record low for the period of 54.98 million lbs set in 1973.
RBH bought late after selling early along with R.J. O'Brien. Refco bought at the low, pit sources said.
